title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A fairly gentle Tuesday: a new breast cancer pill got FDA approval, Senegal got its soccer trophy back, and Massachusetts turkeys reminded everyone who really runs Thanksgiving week. Closer to home in the Carolinas, watch the weather if you're traveling Wednesday night, and keep an eye on talk of I-77 toll lanes reaching into York County.

stories.headline: Charge dropped against NC Congresswoman-elect LaKesha Womack
stories.summary: Mecklenburg County's district attorney has dismissed a felony charge against Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack (D) over a rental car that wasn't returned in 2019. Womack paid Budget for the overdue rental period, and the company said it didn't want to prosecute and considered the matter resolved. Womack has said she was experiencing homelessness at the time.
key_facts: The car was rented Aug. 27, 2019 and recovered by law enforcement Dec. 4, 2019.
The charge was filed in 2020, but the warrant wasn't served until October 2026, during her campaign.
The dismissal is 'with prejudice,' meaning it can't be refiled.
Womack, a 49-year-old minister and consultant, defeated Republican Rep. Tim Moore in the 14th District.
stories.why: It clears up an open legal question for the incoming representative of a district covering parts of Mecklenburg, Gaston, Cleveland and Burke counties.

stories.headline: Rain and wind may slow Thanksgiving travel, then sunshine for Black Friday
stories.summary: A coastal storm, expected to become a nor'easter, is set to bring rain and strong winds to the Carolinas on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. The heaviest rain should come Wednesday evening into Thanksgiving morning, with things improving Thursday afternoon. The West Coast is also dealing with Pacific storms.
key_facts: AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel 50+ miles for Thanksgiving, Nov. 24-30.
The FAA warns rain could affect flights across the Southeast on Wednesday.
Weather has caused 60% of flight delays so far this year, per FAA data.
Charlotte Douglas Airport will post major disruptions on social media.
stories.why: If you can leave early or build in extra time, now's the moment, and the weekend looks sunny.

stories.headline: Army plans careful disposal of old explosives in Iowa, with lead-safety steps
stories.summary: The U.S. Army planned to detonate about 5 tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, saying the material had become too unstable to keep or move. Officials described extensive measures like sand barriers, screening and soaking the ground to keep lead dust from spreading, and released maps of possible exposure areas. Local residents and health advocates have voiced concerns.
key_facts: The Army's stated goal is 'zero release' of lead particles into the air.
In a 1977 Colorado disposal of about 7,000 pounds, the Army says 75% of the lead stayed on site with no mitigation.
Iowa Poison Control's Dr. Dan McCabe says children, pregnant people and malnourished people are the highest-risk groups.
McCabe notes there's no safe level of lead in the body, so caregivers should be extra careful with kids' hand-to-mouth habits.
disputed: How much lead will actually escape is not yet known; officials and health experts say they are hopeful the mitigation will sharply reduce it.
stories.why: Clear public health guidance is available for nearby families, and officials say they've taken unusually extensive precautions.

stories.headline: I-77 toll 'choice lanes' could stretch into York County
stories.summary: South Carolina transportation leaders are exploring optional toll lanes on I-77 that would connect to North Carolina's planned express lanes and run about three miles into York County, possibly to Gold Hill Road in Fort Mill. The free lanes would stay as they are. It's very early, and residents have mixed feelings, with some preferring a wider interstate or more mass transit.
key_facts: A new South Carolina law now allows 'choice lanes.'
Tolls would vary by traffic and time of day.
About 40,000 York County residents commute into Charlotte daily, per Rock Hill Mayor John Gettys.
Both states would need to agree on costs and toll collection; public comment is promised.
stories.why: If you commute on I-77 south of Charlotte, this could shape your future drive, and there will be chances to weigh in.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang apologizes to staff after returning as CEO
stories.summary: Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees he 'made some terrible mistakes' and is in therapy, in his first all-hands meeting since being reinstated as CEO. He resigned Nov. 12 over extramarital affairs and was brought back after the company said the U.S. government told it he wasn't a national security risk. Nvidia stock jumped over 30% Monday, then fell about 6% Tuesday.
key_facts: Huang resigned Nov. 12 and was reinstated Monday.
President Trump told CNBC he spoke with the board and 'convinced them'; Huang dismissed suggestions he returned due to pressure.
Trump owned as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of Sept. 30, per filings.
disputed: Confirmed: Huang resigned, was reinstated, and apologized (per The New York Times' review of the livestream).
Reported: one affair was with a suspected Chinese spy; Nvidia says the government found Huang wasn't a security risk.
Unclear: how much Trump's contact with the board influenced the decision; Huang and Trump describe it differently.
Huang also faces probes whose outcome isn't known.
stories.why: Nvidia is central to the AI boom, so its leadership drama ripples through the wider stock market.

stories.headline: First new hormone pill for early breast cancer in 20+ years gets FDA approval
stories.summary: The FDA approved Roche's Wilserdly, an oral pill, for use after surgery in people with intermediate- to high-risk ER-positive, HER2-negative early-stage breast cancer. It's the first new hormone therapy option in this setting in more than two decades. In a large trial, it lowered the risk of the cancer coming back or death by 30% compared with standard therapy.
key_facts: Three-year invasive disease-free survival: 92.4% with Wilserdly vs 89.6% with tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors.
Backed by the phase 3 lidERA trial.
About 225,000 U.S. patients are diagnosed with HR+/HER2- breast cancer each year; nearly 90% are caught early.
Days earlier, it was also approved with everolimus for some advanced, ESR1-mutated cases.
disputed: FDA approved, based on a phase 3 trial.
Approved for a specific group: post-surgery, intermediate to high risk, ER+/HER2- early-stage disease.
The drug did not succeed in a separate first-line metastatic breast cancer trial.
stories.why: It's a meaningful new option for one of the most common forms of breast cancer after a long stretch with none.

stories.headline: Senegal gets its Africa Cup of Nations title back
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously ruled that Senegal won January's AFCON final, reversing a decision that had handed the title to Morocco after Senegalese players briefly walked off over a penalty. The court said that because the referee restarted the match, the forfeit rules didn't apply, so Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win stands.
key_facts: It's Senegal's second African title, after 2022.
CAF had awarded Morocco a 3-0 win in March.
Sadio Mane said the ruling 'fills us with joy' and sent respect to Moroccan fans and players.
Morocco says it will pursue further legal options, citing alleged contact between an arbitrator and Senegal's federation president.
stories.why: It settles the on-field result, for now, and Mane's message of friendship between the two countries was a nice touch.

stories.headline: Copa America returns to the U.S. in 2028
stories.summary: The Copa America will be played in the United States from June 9 to July 9, 2028, right before the Los Angeles Olympics. It's the second straight U.S.-hosted edition, with 16 teams from South and North America.
key_facts: All 10 South American nations plus six North American teams that qualify via the 2027 Gold Cup.
Olympic men's soccer starts July 10, hours after the Copa final.
Host cities will be announced later.
stories.why: U.S. soccer fans get another big summer of top-level games close to home.
